The label spells the second arranger Koenemann. The arrangement, not an anonymous unarranged folk performance, is heard.

Processing
Transferred at 78 rpm using four truncated-conical styli: 3.8, 2.3, 2.8 and 3.3 mil. The named MP3 derives from the archive’s preferred FLAC. Documented

Surface noise and transfer equalisation prevent absolute sound-quality or loudness comparisons.

[1]
Composition rights
Traditional melody; Chaliapin–Keneman arrangement is public domain under ordinary life-plus-70 terms Inferred, not documented

DAHR identifies the arrangers as Chaliapin (1873–⁠1938) and Keneman (1873–⁠1937). No claim of worldwide clearance is made.

[1] [3]
Recording rights
US public domain: sound recording published before the 1925 cutoff Documented

The inspected Victrola label reads 88663 and credits both arrangers. IA repeats 88663 in its matrix field; DAHR identifies the actual matrix as Cc1891, take 4. DAHR’s [1922] publication year is explicitly bracketed. No non-commercial licence is present in the inspected archive metadata.
